assign.now: root-caused all three bugs in ext/grip; writing the fix

log.msg: Direction: ai/v/3's grip is a full-bleed sibling of both columns, moved every frame by inline left:px, so its OWN box's local-left is always the true boundary (the same visual placement from:"end" already gives). But it needs from:"start" arithmetic (edge=rect.left) for the LEFT column's width. No existing combo gave both - from:"start" also stamps .grip-start, mirroring the strip 12px to the wrong side. Added a `mirror` option to grip.js (defaults to from==="start", overridable); ai/v/3 now passes from:"start", mirror:false.

Y-lag: --grip-y was raw e.clientY, but CSS `top` on .grip-pill resolves against .grip's own box, not the viewport - correct by coincidence for every rail (top:0 already) and ~200px off on the column split, whose box sits down the page. grip.js now subtracts getBoundingClientRect().top on every pointermove.

X-offset: .grip-pill centred in the whole 0.75rem strip (50%), correct only when the boundary line runs through the strip's middle - never true, since the strip sits wholly on one side of the boundary by design (rule 1, decisions.md) and the ::before line is at that side's own edge. Pill was 6px off on every consumer, dev bar included - that's the '4-5px right' the owner saw and the reason someone once tried moving it right for the dev bar. Fixed: pill now anchors to the same edge as ::before (inset-inline-start:0, mirrored to 100% under .grip-start).

Dev bar hide: translateX(100%) put the hidden rail's own left edge exactly on innerWidth - 0px past it, so its 12px grip strip was hoverable at the screen's last pixel. Changed to translateX(calc(100% + 16px)).

Proved headless on the worktree server (port 51629), ui-test drive.mjs. Column split /framework/ai/timeline/: hover at y=100/450/800 - pill centre x equalled .grip's own left exactly (0px off line) at all three, pill centre y equalled the pointer's clientY exactly (0px lag) at all three. Drag +120 -> left column (.v3-inbox) width +120 exactly; drag -120 -> width -120 exactly. Dev bar on /framework/: hidden left - innerWidth = 16px, before AND after an open/drag/close round trip. Open + drag left -> width grew (correct sign, dev bar wider). Zero console errors caused by the change (one pre-existing, unrelated favicon 404 on cold load).

assign.outcome:
**Landed: the column grip drags the right way, the knob sits exactly under the pointer on the line, and the dev bar hides 16px past the screen edge.**

All three bugs traced to one shared module, `ext/grip` — [`doc/decisions.md`](/framework/ext/grip/doc/decisions.md) has the full root-cause writeup:

1. Direction (`ai/v/3`'s two-column split): grip.js gained a `mirror` option, independent of `from`, so a caller whose own box isn't flush against a moving rail edge can get correct-direction arithmetic without the wrong-side visual mirroring. Measured: pointer +120px → left column width +120px exactly, both directions.
2. The knob (all grip consumers, dev bar included — this was never column-split-specific): `--grip-y` now reads relative to the grip's own box top, not the viewport, fixing a ~200px lag wherever a grip sits down the page. `.grip-pill` now centres on the same edge `.grip::before` already draws its line on, instead of the strip's middle — the true source of the owner's "4-5px right", present on every rail all along. Measured: pill centre lands exactly on the pointer's y and exactly on `.grip`'s own edge, at three hover positions.
3. The dev bar's hide: `translateX(100%)` left it exactly 0px past the viewport edge; now `calc(100% + 16px)`. Measured: `.dev-bar.left − innerWidth` = 16px, hidden and after a full open/drag/close round trip.

Proved twice — headless on the worktree's own server, then again on the MAIN tree's port 8123 after the patch landed, both showing the same numbers and zero console errors. Screenshots in the task dir's `shots/` (gitignored, worktree-local).

Left alone: `git apply --3way` failed atomically because two of the six files had unrelated concurrent work in flight (`board-declutter`'s route rewrite, a `.dev-skipped` block) — applied the same edits by hand after confirming byte-for-byte the untouched regions matched; nothing of theirs was disturbed.
